- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overcorrects downward; delay or dampen the correction to allow for mean reversion.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending up, model may underreact; increase forecast slightly to capture momentum.
- Model consistently underestimates late-period price surges (especially >80) when sentiment is bullish; add a small upward bias for final 5–7 days.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-period, model often fails to adjust; apply a lagged correction: reduce forecast by 1–2% per day of sentiment decay.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overfit short-term volatility; smooth out extreme swings by applying a 3–5 day moving average filter on forecast deviations.
